accepted_scope_caveats.label: lem:identification-fwl and all causal downstream statements
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Event-date cohort-average transport is an untestable counterfactual cross-date premise, not a consequence of the observed historical panel.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Identification, estimation, lower-bound, and interval claims are conditional on ass:event-transport; rolling pseudo-events only diagnose pre-event stability.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: lem:joint-law-embedding, thm:sharp-joint-frontier, and thm:honest-length-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The lower covariance-standardized local modulus needed for the donor lower channel is maintained rather than derived from the Hölder ball.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The N^{-min(lambda,1)} donor converse and all matched-frontier claims are conditional on ass:local-two-sided-modulus; because this focal channel is assumed, the proposal is capped at field tier.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies causal financial event studies, derives identification and asymptotic-bias conditions under factor-model misspecification, and proposes synthetic-control alternatives; it does not state a generated-center minimax or honest-length result.
The paper studies nonparametric repeated-measurement regression over Hölder spaces, derives nearly optimal rates and a sampling-frequency phase transition under clustered dependence.
The paper estimates a unique minimizer and minimum value of a smooth strongly convex regression function using a local-polynomial-based two-stage procedure and proves upper and minimax lower bounds.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1865-1867, Introduction and Section 2; Appendix A description
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article constructs conditional synthetic-control prediction intervals, separates weight-estimation and post-treatment uncertainty, and extends its construction to weakly dependent beta-mixing time series in Appendix A.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear regression functionals over convex classes under normal errors with known variance.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a scalar worked submodel that calculates the four information channels, the donor modulus, and the interval radius directly from observable primitives; it would make the joint-law embedding's economic interpretation easier to audit.
State a finite-sample selected-Gram success probability and retained-block fallback bound under the declared density and mixing constants, rather than leaving all fallback control asymptotic.

Develop a comparator theorem on one common replicated-site submodel contrasting exact training coordinates, generated evaluation centers, and classical noisy training coordinates, with a sharp condition for when the donor-modulus channel replaces deconvolution.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with both accepted conditional-scope caveats fixed; prioritize construction of the four channelwise joint causal-panel lower-bound submodels and the retained-block interval proof.
